name: Italy
tagline: Public tuition set by family income, so it can be almost free
summary: Italy has no single national application system for EU students. You apply to each university on its own portal, and for many degrees you also sit an online entrance test called a TOLC. The big surprise is money: public universities charge you according to your family's income, not a flat fee, so a family on a normal income often pays a few hundred to a couple of thousand euros a year. English-taught bachelor's degrees exist but are a minority, concentrated in economics, engineering, design and international relations.
whyConsider: Public university fees are income-based (ISEE), so the bill can be €0 to a few hundred euros for lower-income families
As an EU citizen you skip the visa and the Universitaly pre-enrolment queue entirely
IB Diploma holders are often exempt from the Dichiarazione di Valore and from translation (San Raffaele says so outright), though the Diploma itself must be apostilled
Strong English-taught clusters: Bocconi and Luiss for economics, the two Politecnici for engineering and design
Living costs outside Milan (Bologna, Padova, Torino, Trento) are low compared with Denmark
watchOuts: Getting the income-based fee as a foreign family means obtaining an ISEE parificato through an Italian CAF office, with your family's income documents legalised and translated — start this months early
If you do not file an ISEE you are automatically put in the top bracket and pay the maximum
Each university runs its own calendar and its own portal; there is no Parcoursup or UCAS to keep you organised
Italy reformed Italian-taught Medicine in 2025 with an open 'semestre filtro'; English-taught Medicine still uses IMAT, but this area is unstable — re-check for 2027 entry
Most bachelor's degrees are still taught in Italian; check language of instruction programme by programme, not university by university

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: Full IB Diploma. No national minimum points figure is confirmed here; individual universities and programmes set their own bar.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: A national IB-to-Italian conversion is not confirmed here. Where a degree has limited places, applicants are ranked by their entrance-test score (TOLC or IMAT), not by IB points.
notes: San Raffaele's guidance for foreign qualifications: 'The Declaration of Value or the Statement of Comparability are NOT required if the qualification obtained is an IB Diploma. The IB Diploma must be Apostilled in all cases' — in Switzerland, where the IB issues it. It also says the DP Course Results certificate is not enough on its own. Other universities set their own document rules.

A CIMEA Statement of Comparability is the modern substitute for the Dichiarazione di Valore for other qualifications; several universities waive it for IB holders who authorise the IB to send results directly via MyIB.
Universitaly states that evaluating foreign qualifications is the exclusive responsibility of each institution, and that credential-evaluation documents are not a compulsory national requirement.
Subject prerequisites are handled by the entrance test rather than by HL/SL rules — a TOLC-I assumes school-level maths and physics, a TOLC-E assumes maths and logic.

portal.name: Universitaly (Ministry portal; pre-enrolment is for visa applicants only)

deadlines.label: Bocconi — Early Session for 2027/28 entry: applications
deadlines.notes: Published on Bocconi's 2027-28 admissions page as "2 - 29 September 2026 (3:00pm Italian time)", with results in mid November 2026. The time given is the closing time. Bocconi runs only two sessions for 2027-28, Early and Winter — the page states "There are two selection sessions available for the admission to the 2027-28 AY: Early and Winter", so unlike earlier years there is no spring round to fall back on.

deadlines.label: Bocconi — Early Session for 2027/28 entry: last date to sit the Bocconi online test
deadlines.notes: Bocconi's 2027-28 admissions page publishes the Early Session test cut-off as "until 24 September 2026" and warns that "the web testing platform will be closed a few days before each application deadline". You must already hold a score — Bocconi online test, SAT, LSAT or ACT — before you can apply, so this falls five days before the application deadline it feeds.

deadlines.label: Bocconi — Winter Session for 2027/28 entry: applications
deadlines.notes: Published as "25 November 2026 - 26 January 2027 (3:00pm Italian time)", with results in mid March 2027. The time given is the closing time. This is the last Bocconi round for 2027-28 entry: there is no spring session.

deadlines.label: Bocconi — Winter Session for 2027/28 entry: last date to sit the Bocconi online test
deadlines.notes: Published as the Winter Session final test date, "21 January 2027", five days before that session's application deadline.

deadlines.label: Visa application for 2027/28, which pre-enrolment on Universitaly must precede (not for EU/EEA or Swiss citizens)
deadlines.notes: Set in the MUR/MAECI circular "Procedure per l'ingresso, il soggiorno, l'immatricolazione degli studenti internazionali", which is explicitly valid for two years: "VALIDE PER GLI ANNI ACCADEMICI 2026-2027 e 2027-2028". Its wording is "Per l'anno accademico 2027/2028 [...] il termine ultimo per la presentazione delle domande di visto è fissato al 31 ottobre 2027"; the 2026/27 equivalent in the same paragraph is "entro e non oltre il 30 novembre 2026". Note what the date actually is: it is the last day to lodge the visa application at the consulate, and the Universitaly pre-enrolment has to be submitted and validated by the university before that — the circular adds that institutions may set their own earlier dates, "Tali date potranno essere anche antecedenti a quella del 30 novembre 2026 e del 31 ottobre 2027". The visa procedure does not apply to EU/EEA or Swiss citizens: the circular lists among those the visa procedures do not apply to "i cittadini appartenenti ai Paesi dell'Unione Europea, nonché a quelli provenienti da Norvegia, Islanda, Lichtenstein e alla Confederazione Elvetica, alla Repubblica di San Marino e alla Santa Sede".

deadlines.label: University-by-university application windows
deadlines.notes: There is no national deadline for EU students, and the MUR circular says so directly: "I termini previsti per le procedure relative alle preiscrizioni ai corsi di studio, ad eccezione di quelli a numero programmato, sono definiti da ogni singola Istituzione della formazione superiore e pubblicati nei rispettivi siti". The selective private and technical universities close much earlier than an IB student expects — Bocconi's first round for 2027/28 closes on 29 September 2026 and has its own entries here. Open-access degrees often accept applications into September of the entry year. Politecnico di Milano had not published its 2027/28 bando for Laurea programmes on 23 September 2026; its most recent call is for 2026/27. Check each university's own admissions page.

deadlines.label: IMAT — entrance test for English-taught Medicine, Dentistry and Veterinary Medicine
deadlines.year: 2027 entry — the 2027 decree does not exist yet
deadlines.notes: The date is set by a ministerial decree published each year, which also fixes the seat numbers and the registration window — Padova states the rule as "The number of places available, the date of the admission test, the content and the procedures for selection are set forth annually by Ministerial Decree". The shape of the rule, from the most recent decree: for 2026/27 entry the decree was D.M. n. 1005 of 6 August 2026, and Bologna's official notice board records that "the International Medical Admission Test (IMAT) will take place on 29 September 2026", citing the MUR notice of 3 July 2026. So the decree lands in early August and the test follows about seven weeks later, at the end of September — after IB results, unlike almost everything else on this page. The 2027 decree had not been issued on 23 September 2026, so no 2027 date exists yet. The 2026 registration window on Universitaly, reported elsewhere as 26 August to 9 September 2026, is not on any official source this page links to, so treat it as unconfirmed.

deadlines.label: TOLC entrance tests
deadlines.notes: CISIA publishes the frequency rule as "Puoi sostenere un TOLC dello stesso tipo ogni mese. Fatto il TOLC, dal giorno dopo puoi prenotarne un altro per il mese successivo", and the season as "Puoi fare il TOLC da febbraio a novembre, entro le scadenze indicate nel bando o avviso di ammissione del corso di laurea che ti interessa" — so the sittings run February to November and each university's own bando sets the last one that counts for its round. There is no single TOLC date to put in a calendar; book early rather than after IB results.

steps: Pick the exact degree programme, not just the university — language of instruction, entrance test and deadline are all set at programme level.

Check whether the programme needs a TOLC (engineering: TOLC-I; economics: TOLC-E; English-taught versions exist) or a university-specific test, and book a sitting early, because you can only take the same TOLC once a calendar month.
Apply on the university's own portal in its admission round, using predicted IB grades where the round closes before July.

Authorise the IB to release your final results to the university through MyIB, or send a copy of the Diploma. Many universities waive the Dichiarazione di Valore for IB holders, but some (San Raffaele, for one) still want the Diploma apostilled in Switzerland — check your university's list.

If you want the income-based fee, apply for an ISEE parificato through an affiliated Italian CAF office, with your family's income and property documents (from wherever they are earned or held) legalised and translated into Italian.
Enrol and pay the first instalment, then confirm your ISEE in time for the second instalment (typically due in spring).
Register your residence with the local comune once you have been in Italy more than three months.
application.selectionNotes: Three different worlds. Open-access degrees admit everyone who passes a non-selective placement test. Numero programmato degrees (national or local) rank applicants by entrance-test score. Private universities such as Bocconi and Luiss run their own selective rounds on school record, test and sometimes interview.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: A meaningful but still minority offer, concentrated in economics and management, engineering, design, international relations and English-taught Medicine. No official national count is given here.
language.englishProof: Universities typically accept IB English A or English B at an agreed grade in place of IELTS/TOEFL, but the accepted grade varies by university, so check each university's page.
notes: Italian is not required for an English-taught degree, but it is required for ordinary life, part-time work and most internships.
The Italian-language proficiency test (TEST@CASA) referred to in Universitaly circulars applies to visa applicants entering Italian-taught programmes, not to EU students on English-taught degrees.

tuitionEuEea.value: Public universities: income-based. Politecnico di Milano 2026/27 charges a first instalment of €880.04 plus a second instalment of €0–€3,003, giving a maximum all-inclusive contribution of about €3,943 a year; students with an ISEE up to €22,000 pay about €157 for the second instalment, and an ISEE below €27,740 reduces the first instalment too. Private universities are flat-rate: Bocconi is €17,000 a year for 2026-27; its 2027-28 amount had not been set on 24 September 2026. Bocconi also cuts that fee by 100%, 80%, 60%, 40% or 20% on need, through one "Bocconi4Access to Education" application.

tuitionNonEu.value: The same income-based scale applies at public universities if an ISEE parificato is filed; without one you are placed in the top bracket and pay the maximum (about €3,943 a year at Politecnico di Milano for 2026/27). Bocconi's fees page gives one figure, €17,000, with no EU/non-EU split.

costs.applicationFee: Varies by university. A TOLC sitting costs €35. Check each university's own fee.
notes: How ISEE works for a foreign family: ISEE is an Italian means-test combining household income (from two years before), savings and property, divided by a scale based on household size. If your family's income and property are outside Italy, you cannot get an ordinary ISEE. Instead you request an ISEE parificato (also written ISEEU parificato) from an affiliated Italian tax-assistance centre, a CAF. You supply household composition, each member's income for the second preceding year, certificates for any property owned on 31 December, and any securities or shareholdings. Foreign documents must be legalised by an Italian diplomatic or consular representation and accompanied by a certified Italian translation. The CAF sends the result straight to the university. If you skip this step, the university assumes you are wealthy and bills the top bracket.

The national 'no tax area' threshold quoted for 2025/26 was an ISEE of €23,000 for full exemption with a taper up to €30,000, but individual universities set their own, often more generous, thresholds (Unimore: full exemption to €27,000, reductions to €45,000; Politecnico di Milano: reduction below €27,740). Always read the university's own regolamento tasse.

Politecnico di Milano warns that an ISEEU parificato does not by itself qualify a student for the statutory partial or total exemptions under Law 232/2016 — a detail worth asking each university about directly.
No official living-cost figure is quoted here.

funding.note: The programme must be SU-approved, and outside the Nordics SU is capped at four years (48 klip).

funding: Regional right-to-study grants (borsa di studio DSU, run by bodies such as DSU Toscana, ER.GO in Emilia-Romagna, EDISU in Piemonte) are means-tested on ISEE and can cover fees, a cash grant and subsidised housing; EU students are eligible on the same terms as Italians.
Bocconi and Luiss both run substantial need-based and merit scholarships assessed on the same income documentation as ISEE.
Erasmus+ funding for an exchange year within the degree.
workRights: EU/EEA citizens have full labour-market access in Italy with no permit and no hour limit. Non-EU students on a study visa are limited to part-time work (commonly cited as 20 hours a week / 1,040 hours a year); check the current limit on the permit.
residency: As an EU/EEA citizen you enter on your passport or national ID card. If you stay longer than three months you register as an EU resident (iscrizione anagrafica) at the comune where you live, showing enrolment, health cover and evidence of sufficient means. You will also want a codice fiscale (tax code) almost immediately — banks, phone contracts, rental agreements and the university all ask for it.
housing: University-owned student housing exists but is limited and usually allocated through the regional right-to-study body on the same means test as the grant. Most students rent a room in a shared flat found through Facebook groups, university noticeboards or agencies. Milan is genuinely expensive and competitive; Bologna, Padova, Torino and Trento are easier. Start looking in June or July for a September start.
healthcare: Bring your European Health Insurance Card for the first months. Students staying long-term usually register voluntarily with the Servizio Sanitario Nazionale for an annual fee, which gives you a family doctor and full access; check the current annual amount with the local health authority.

institutions.name: Bocconi University
institutions.englishBachelors: Most bachelor programmes are taught in English
institutions.note: A private university for economics, finance and management, taught mostly in English. Its two selective rounds for 2027-28 close on 29 September 2026 (Early) and 26 January 2027 (Winter), and an income-based waiver ladder can cut the €17,000 fee (2026-27) sharply.

institutions.name: Politecnico di Milano
institutions.englishBachelors: Several English-taught bachelor programmes in engineering and design
institutions.note: A technical university with income-based fees, up to a published maximum of about €3,943 a year.

institutions.name: Politecnico di Torino
institutions.englishBachelors: A number of English-taught engineering bachelors
institutions.note: Turin's engineering school, close to the Italian car and aerospace industry, and cheaper to live in than Milan.

institutions.name: University of Bologna
institutions.englishBachelors: A growing set of English-taught first-cycle degrees
institutions.note: Founded in 1088, in a lively and welcoming student city.

institutions.name: Sapienza University of Rome
institutions.englishBachelors: Some English-taught bachelor programmes, including English-taught Medicine
institutions.note: Enormous, historic and central, with English-taught Medicine entered through IMAT.

institutions.name: University of Padua
institutions.note: A serious research university in a compact, walkable student town half an hour from Venice.

institutions.name: University of Trento
institutions.englishBachelors: Comparative, European and International Legal Studies is taught in English; Computer Science, Economics and Management, Biomolecular Sciences and a communications-engineering degree are taught in English and Italian
institutions.note: Small and alpine, with Comparative, European and International Legal Studies taught in English, and computer science and economics in English and Italian.

institutions.name: Luiss Guido Carli
institutions.englishBachelors: Most bachelor programmes available in English
institutions.note: Private, well connected to Italian business and politics, and the usual alternative to Bocconi for anyone who wants Rome.

institutions.name: Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore
institutions.englishBachelors: Nine three-year bachelor's taught in English, including Economics and Management, Finance, International Relations and Global Affairs, and Psychology, plus English-taught Medicine in Rome and Bolzano
institutions.note: A private Catholic university with campuses in Milan, Rome, Brescia and Piacenza. Applications for 2027/28 open in autumn 2026; an IB score of 31 or more makes you a priority applicant.

institutions.name: University of Milano-Bicocca
institutions.note: A young public university in northern Milan, far cheaper than the private schools in the same city.

institutions.name: Ca' Foscari University of Venice
institutions.note: Strong in languages, Asian studies and economics, in a city that is hard to live in cheaply.

institutions.name: University of Milan
institutions.englishBachelors: A small English-taught offer including English-taught Medicine
institutions.note: Milan's large public research university, and another IMAT entry point for English-taught Medicine.

institutions.name: University of Turin
institutions.note: A large, old public university in a city with lower rents than Milan and an unusually good public-transport and food culture.
